authority_note: Owner chose 'cách 1' (option 1): stage-1 sends NO identifier fields — only non-PII event-level fields. Because stage-1 emits NO personal data to any external platform, this is a fail-closed MEASUREMENT-CONFIG decision, NOT a PII-egress decision, so no privacy/legal (Sếp) sign-off is required for stage-1. Opening ANY identifier field (email/phone/external_id) to Meta later is a SEPARATE decision that DOES require privacy/legal — see still_open.
decision: Stage-1 external-send FIELD policy: when an event is (later) classified ALLOW_EXTERNAL, ONLY non-PII event-level fields may be sent — event_name, event_time, event_id, value, currency, content_ids/SKU, action_source. NO identifier field (em/ph/external_id/psid) is sent in stage-1. HASH method RESERVED for a future identifier-field opening: normalize (lowercase, trim, phone E.164 without +) then SHA-256 hex; external_id would be M6's existing psid_hash (HMAC + M6 pepper); no raw PII ever. Offline conversion follows the same rule and only when opened.
still_open: Opening ANY identifier field (em/ph/external_id) to Meta = a future explicit decision requiring privacy/legal (Sếp). Until then identifier fields stay closed (not sent).
conditions: stage-1 emits NO PII externally; no identifier field is sent
no field opening flips a flag: external_send stays Final OFF; production_flag OFF; global_gateway_state BLOCKED
no event is ALLOW_EXTERNAL yet (permit-mapping is a separate item); this decision only bounds WHICH FIELDS may be sent when an event is eventually opened
when identifier fields are later opened, that decision goes to privacy/legal (Sếp) and this reserved Meta-CAPI hash method applies
